tagline: Operate the Miren PaaS from an agent: deploy apps, run the server, and debug them
description_md:
Miren is a deployment platform for small teams. This app is the app-store front door for the `miren` CLI, letting an agent drive a Miren PaaS over IPC.

What an agent gets:
- **Deploy lifecycle** — `miren.deploy` (non-interactive build + deploy), `miren.deploy.analyze` (detect the stack/services without building), and `miren.rollback`.
- **Inspect apps** — `miren.apps`, `miren.app` (status), `miren.app.history`, and `miren.logs` (JSON).
- **Server & diagnostics** — `miren.server.install`/`miren.server.status`, `miren.doctor`, `miren.whoami`, and `miren.debug.connection`/`miren.debug.advertise`.
- **Full CLI surface** — `miren.exec` runs any verbatim `miren` argv (addon, auth, env, route, cluster, disk, sandbox, and more).

Good to know:
- Structured JSON is returned wherever the CLI offers it (e.g. pass `--json`).
- Discover the live surface at runtime with `miren.help` — every method, its parameters, and its latency class (fast / med / slow).
- Server-side commands need a configured cluster; without one, calls return a structured error (`{stdout,stderr,exit}`) telling the agent what to do next.
- Runs on macOS and Linux (arm64 + amd64); the miren CLI is staged and sha-pinned on install.

methods.name: miren.exec
methods.summary: Run any miren subcommand. Payload is {"args":[...]} — the verbatim miren argv. Use this for the full CLI surface beyond the curated methods below (addon, auth, env, route, cluster, disk, sandbox, etc.). Run `miren help` or `miren <command> --help` for the surface. Example args: ["app","list","--json"]. Note: interactive subcommands (e.g. `app run`, `login`) and long-running ones (e.g. `server start`) are not suitable over IPC.

methods.name: miren.apps
methods.summary: List all applications on the cluster (alias for `app list`).

methods.name: miren.app
methods.summary: Show the current status of one application. Provide the app name.

methods.name: miren.logs
methods.summary: Read recent logs for an application as JSON.

methods.name: miren.deploy
methods.summary: Build and deploy the app in the current directory (non-interactive, --force).

methods.name: miren.deploy.analyze
methods.summary: Analyze the app's detected stack/services without building or deploying.

methods.name: miren.rollback
methods.summary: Roll an application back to its previous deployed version.

methods.name: miren.doctor
methods.summary: Diagnose the miren environment and connectivity.

methods.name: miren.whoami
methods.summary: Show the current authenticated user and cluster.

methods.name: miren.server.install
methods.summary: Install the miren server as a systemd service on this host (Linux only).

methods.name: miren.server.status
methods.summary: Show miren server service status (Linux only).

methods.name: miren.debug.connection
methods.summary: Test connectivity and authentication with the miren server.

methods.name: miren.debug.advertise
methods.summary: Show which addresses the server would advertise and why.

methods.name: miren.help
methods.summary: Discovery: every method with params, kind, and latency class.

Notes: Operate the Miren PaaS from an agent: deploy and roll back apps; inspect status, logs, and history; run the server; and diagnose connectivity — plus a passthrough exec for any miren subcommand.

examples.title: Roll back to the previous version

gotchas: Server-side commands need a configured cluster; without one they return a structured {stdout,stderr,exit} error explaining the next step — not a crash.
miren.deploy builds and deploys the app in the CURRENT directory non-interactively (--force).
Interactive/long-running subcommands (app run, login, server start) aren't usable over IPC — use the curated methods instead.
Pass --json inside miren.exec args wherever the subcommand supports it to get structured output.
server install / server status are Linux-only.

edges.why: miren has no cluster to talk to yet — every command soft-fails like this with exit 0, so read the envelope's stdout/stderr, not the exit code

then.why: point miren at your cluster — the one setup step that unblocks every other method (`miren login` is interactive and unusable over IPC)
prints exactly which of config/server/auth is still missing, plus the get-started commands

edges.why: a required param was omitted — the app/name param must be an application that exists on your cluster

then.why: lists the applications on the cluster so you can pass a real one as name (miren.app) or app (miren.logs)
